forms: pick the string instrument from a list
say how it is played
match an instrument to its community
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G6.CREATI.STRING_MUSICAL_INSTRUMEN..mastery: The child names the nyatiti and the orutu (Luo), the litungu (Luhya) and the obokano (Gusii) as string instruments, says that the nyatiti, litungu and obokano are plucked and the orutu is played with a bow, and does not put a drum or a flute in the string group. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the part from its job
say what the strings, the body and the pegs each do
say how to raise the sound
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G6.CREATI.STRING_MUSICAL_INSTRUMEN..mastery: The child says the strings vibrate to make the sound, the hollow body makes the sound louder, the bridge holds the strings above the body and passes their shaking to it, the pegs tighten or loosen the strings to tune them, a tighter string gives a higher sound, and the bow of the orutu rubs the string to make it sound. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the picture made with dots
say how dots make dark and light
put the stippling steps in order
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G6.CREATI.STRING_MUSICAL_INSTRUMEN..mastery: The child says stippling is drawing a picture with many small dots, that dots packed close together look dark and dots spaced apart look light, that no lines or smudging are used, and puts the steps in order: light pencil outline, dots with a pen, closer dots for dark parts. This is the knowledge half of outcomes d and e; drawing is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the primary colours
say which two colours make a secondary colour
sort a colour as warm or cool
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G6.CREATI.PAINTING_AND_COLLAGE.COLO.mastery: The child names red, yellow and blue as primary colours, says orange (red and yellow), green (yellow and blue) and violet (blue and red) are secondary colours, that a tertiary colour is a primary mixed with the secondary beside it, and sorts red, orange and yellow as warm and blue, green and violet as cool. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say what a still life is
pick the use of a mat
say how a collage is made
put the mounting steps in order
CREA.G6.CREATI.PAINTING_AND_COLLAGE.TECH.mastery: The child says a still life is a painting of objects that do not move (a bowl of fruit, a jug), that brush strokes are the marks the brush leaves, that a mat is a card border put round a painting when it is mounted for display, and that a collage is made by gluing pieces of paper, cloth or other materials on a surface. Painting and mounting are practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the way to serve
pick the part of the body used to dig
say a rule of the game
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G6.CREATI.VOLLEYBALL.SKILLS.mastery: The child says a team has six players on the court, the under-arm serve is struck from below the waist with the fist or open hand so that the ball goes over the net, a dig pass uses the joined forearms (or one hand) to lift a low ball, and the ball must not be caught, kicked or held. This is the knowledge half of outcomes a to c; playing is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say how many beats a note lasts
say what a rest means
count a three-beat bar
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G6.CREATI.RHYTHM_AND_PATTERN_MAKIN..mastery: The child says a semibreve lasts four beats, a minim two, a crotchet one and a quaver half a beat (two quavers make one beat), that a rest is a silence of the same length as its note, and that in a three-beat pattern each bar adds up to three beats. Clapping and improvising are practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: put the steps in order
say what a motif is
say what a full repeat pattern is
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G6.CREATI.RHYTHM_AND_PATTERN_MAKIN..mastery: The child says a motif is a single shape used in a design (a circle, a triangle or a square), puts the steps in order (draw the motif on the block, cut it away so the motif stands up, roll ink on the block, press it on the paper, lift it, repeat in a row) and says a repeat pattern uses the same motif over and over in even rows. Cutting and printing are practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the warp or the weft
say how a plain weave goes
pick the materials
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G6.CREATI.WEAVING.PLAIN_WEAVE.mastery: The child says the warp is the set of threads held tight on the loom and the weft is the thread woven across them, that plain weave goes over one warp and under the next and the next row does the opposite, that a serrated card loom has notches to hold the warp, and names suitable materials (raffia, sisal, strips of cloth, wool). Weaving a mat is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: put the cartwheel hands and feet in order
say what makes a good cartwheel
put the sequence in order
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G6.CREATI.GYMNASTICS.CARTWHEEL.mastery: The child says a cartwheel is a sideways turn with straight arms, in the order hand, hand, foot, foot, with the legs straight and wide, that a forward roll tucks the chin and rounds the back, that a swan balance stands on one leg with the other leg lifted behind and arms out, and puts the sequence cartwheel, forward roll, swan balance in order. Performing is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say the next syllable
say the syllables going down
say which sounds higher
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G6.CREATI.MELODY.SOLFA.mastery: The child says the syllables going up are doh, re, mi, fah, soh, lah, ti, doh1 and going down are doh1, ti, lah, soh, fah, mi, re, doh, that doh1 sounds higher than doh, that the hand sign for doh is a closed fist and for ti a finger pointing up. Singing, signing and composing are practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: put the phases in order
say how to take off
say what the sail and the scissors are
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G6.PERFOR.ATHLETICS.JUMPS.mastery: The child puts the long jump phases in order (run-up, take-off from one foot, flight, landing in the pit), says the sail is holding the legs together and forward in the air, that the high jump starts from an angled run-up, takes off on one foot, goes over the bar in a scissors action (one leg and then the other) and lands on the mat, and that a long jump is measured to the nearest mark in the sand. Performing is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: pick the way to hold it
say how to blow and tongue
say what covered holes do
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G6.PERFOR.DESCANT_RECORDER.TECHNIQU.mastery: The child says the left hand is on the top holes and the right hand below, the thumb covers the hole at the back, the finger pads cover the holes fully, the player blows gently and tongues each note with "too", and covering more holes gives a lower sound. The national anthem begins "Ee Mungu nguvu yetu". Playing is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: sort an instrument into percussion, wind or string
pick what a good ensemble player does
say why players listen
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G6.PERFOR.INDIGENOUS_KENYAN_INSTRU..mastery: The child sorts drums, shakers and rattles as percussion, horns and flutes as wind and the nyatiti and litungu as string, says an ensemble can be of one kind or mixed, and says that players in an ensemble keep a steady beat, listen to each other, balance their loudness and start and stop together. Playing is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: put the steps in order
say how to join two pieces
say how to dry and decorate
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G6.PERFOR.INDIGENOUS_KENYAN_CRAFT_..mastery: The child says a slab is a flat sheet of clay rolled out to an even thickness, puts the steps in order (roll the slab, cut the pieces, score and wet the edges, press them together, smooth, dry slowly, decorate), says joining needs scratching and slip (clay mixed with water) and that clay dried too fast cracks. Modelling a vase is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: say how the body lies
say how the legs kick
say when to breathe
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G6.PERFOR.SWIMMING.BREASTSTROKE.mastery: The child says the body lies flat and face down, the arms sweep out, in and forward, the legs do a frog kick (knees bend, feet turn out, kick back and together), the head lifts to breathe at the end of the arm pull and the swimmer glides, and that a child swims only with a trained adult watching. Swimming is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

forms: name the element from its job
say what the message of a song is
sort a song's message
find the false step in a learner's answer
CREA.G6.APPREC.ANALYSIS_OF_CREATIVE_ART..mastery: The child says pitch is how high or low a sound is, tempo is how fast or slow, dynamics is how loud or soft, rhythm is the pattern of long and short sounds, melody is the tune, and that a message is what the words of a song teach or say (about unity, work, peace, care of the environment). Judging a real song is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.

CREA.G6.APPREC.ANALYSIS_OF_CREATIVE_ART..mastery: The child says a catalogue is a list of the artworks in an exhibition, each entry gives a number, the title, the artist, the material and the size, and it helps visitors find and understand the works. Making a catalogue (outcome a) is practical. Evidence rule: at least four of the last five fresh questions right across at least two question forms, and no repeated pick of the same misconception.
